text:
mike.b: Heads up — noticed p95/p99 for /v1/generate flipped between region-a and region-b after we changed routing weights this morning. charts look like region-b got worse but aggregate stayed similar. anyone seen this?
anna: ugh, can you paste the console query you used? screenshot helps too. :eyes: 
mike.b: query from dashboard:
```
SELECT percentile(latency_ms, [50,95,99]) FROM endpoint_latency WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND window=5m GROUP BY region
```
link: https://console/redwood/dashboard/latency?route=%2Fv1%2Fgenerate
joel: did we change fallback routing or add a variant in region-b? small variant differences can move tail a lot.
sara: probable explanation: our rollup merge uses tdigest and we recently enabled cross-region rollup for that dataset. tdigest merge is approximate and sensitive to low-sample buckets — if region-b has few samples at high-latency tail, p99 can jump after mix.
kevin: what's the sample count per-region? that will tell if it's just noise or a real regression.
mike.b: counts: region-a=12.4k, region-b=480, total=12.88k. so region-b is low.
anna: that explains it. low sample + tdigest cross-rollup = unstable p99. we should surface sample_count on the pctl tooltip and maybe gray out pctl when count < X.
joel: agree. Also we could: 1) switch rollup merge mode to 'per-route' for production endpoints, or 2) expose a provenance badge (source: client/server/kvcache) so console users see origin.
sara: ops note: deploy-bot shows rollout at 08:12 UTC changed route-weight for region-b -> +10%. that bumped more requests into the low-sample pool briefly.
deploy-bot: rollout "routing-weight-adjustment" succeeded at 08:12 UTC — 6 hosts updated.
kevin: for immediate triage we should add sample_count overlay on p95/p99 lines and a warning when samples < 1k. can someone file a quick UX ticket?
anna: i'll file one and add a mock for tooltip. assigning to eng-platform-ux.
mike.b: thanks — for short term i'll annotate the dashboard with a note and pin this thread to the route slack. :thumbsup:
sara: long-term: we should add a 'stable-percentile' mode that uses deterministic histogram buckets for tail when sample counts are low. filing RFC next week.
joel: sounds good. also add a small blurb in the rollout runbook: "monitor per-region sample_count before changing weights >5%".
kevin: +1
anna: added ticket: https://issues/redwood/ENGPLAT-7890 — includes mock, acceptance: show sample_count, add tooltip warning, and toggle to per-route merge.
mike.b: great, leaving this pinned. thanks all!
